name: Plumping gloss (menthol / cinnamon)
lead: Lip plumpers are cosmetics that make lips look fuller by irritating the lip skin and causing temporary swelling [1]. Wikipedia names capsaicin, the compound in chili peppers, as an ingredient; it does not discuss menthol or cinnamon-based products specifically [1].
No clinical studies of irritant plumping glosses were found, and no looksmaxxing-community sources were available for this entry.

paras: According to Wikipedia, lip plumpers work through irritation of the lip skin that produces swelling and a temporarily fuller look [1]. The same article places them within a broader history of lip augmentation that includes early paraffin attempts, liquid silicone in the 1960s and bovine collagen from about 1980 [1].

card.summary: Irritant glosses that swell lips for a short-lived fuller look; little formal research behind them.

quick.overview:
Plumping glosses contain ingredients that irritate the lips, which temporarily swell and look fuller. The effect is short-lived.

No clinical studies were found.
quick.mechanism: Irritation of the lip skin produces mild swelling, according to Wikipedia.
quick.risks: Since the mechanism is irritation, redness or discomfort can be expected; no studies of adverse events specific to these products were found.
